text: {"question":"How does the model ensure the stability of the heavy dark quark, and what role does the absence of a weak interaction analogue play in this stability?","reference_answer":"The heavy dark quark remains stable because the dark sector lacks a weak‑like interaction that could mediate its decay; without such a force, the heavy quark cannot transition to lighter states and thus persists as a stable component of dark matter.","passage_1_contribution":"The abstract states that the heavy dark matter can evade existing constraints on self‑interactions while containing rich phenomenology.","passage_2_contribution":"The conclusions explain that the heavy dark quark is stable because the dark sector has no equivalent of the weak interaction, preventing its decay.","joint_reason":"The stability claim is introduced in the abstract but the mechanism—absence of a weak interaction analogue—is detailed in the conclusions.","same_quantity":false}
